sources.shortCitation: Ufa board minutes on Jewish staff, 29 March 1933
sources.fullCitation: “Über die Weiterbeschäftigung von jüdischen Mitarbeitern und Angestellten.” Niederschrift der Ufa-Vorstandssitzung vom 29. März 1933, quoted from Klaus Kreimeier, Die UFA Story: Geschichte eines Filmkonzerns (Munich and Vienna, 1992), p. 248. DFF – Deutsches Filminstitut & Filmmuseum / filmportal.de.
sources.researchNote: The minutes record the resolution itself: that contracts with Jewish staff were to be dissolved wherever possible, each board member deciding who was to go at once and who “im Wege eines langsamen Abbaues”, and then naming individual cases from Charell and Pommer to the office staff. filmportal.de gives the text with the note “Zitiert nach” Kreimeier 1992, p. 248, so the wording reaches this record through that book rather than from the Ufa files, and the reliability is set accordingly. The date is the date of the sitting, stated in the document’s own heading.
sources.title: Ufa board minutes on the dismissal of Jewish staff

timelineEvents.title: Ufa resolves to terminate the contracts of its Jewish staff
timelineEvents.label: 29 March 1933 · Ufa board resolution
timelineEvents.shortDescription: One day after Goebbels addressed the film industry at the Hotel Kaiserhof, the Ufa board resolved to end the contracts of its Jewish staff.
timelineEvents.longDescription: On 28 March 1933 Joseph Goebbels addressed representatives of the film industry at the Hotel Kaiserhof in Berlin. The next day the board of Universum-Film AG resolved in principle that contracts with its Jewish employees were to be terminated wherever possible, each board member deciding who in his department was to go at once and who was to be removed “im Wege eines langsamen Abbaues”, through a gradual reduction. The resolution was not limited to German citizens, so it reached Kaper and Jurmann as well, and its effect on their work was visible during the production of Kind, ich freu’ mich auf Dein Kommen.
